title: Generation of 3D ex vivo mouse- and patient-derived glioma explant slice model for integration of confocal time-lapse imaging and spatial analysis
protocol: Anesthetize one-day-old C57BL/6 mouse pups via hypothermia for 2 min.
Place the anesthetized pups in a stereotaxic apparatus.
Orthotopically inject plasmid combination into the subventricular zone of neonatal pups using jetPEI® for transfection.
Monitor tumor evolution weekly using IVIS® Spectrum imaging system to measure bioluminescence.
Assess tumor burden with behavioral monitoring regularly.
Euthanize animals when reaching humane endpoint criteria or IVIS signal of 106 to 107 photon/seconds.
Confirm the presence of a tumor using an epifluorescent stereomicroscope before proceeding further.
Dissociate the cultured neurospheres with StemPro Accutase.
Resuspend dissociated neurospheres in DMEM F-12 without FBS or supplements, achieving a final concentration of 50,000 cells/μL.
Anesthetize mice using ketamine at 120 mg/kg and dexmedetomidine at 0.5 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injection.
Provide preemptive analgesia by subcutaneous injection of carprofen at 5 mg/kg.
Shave the heads of anesthetized mice before securing them in a stereotaxic apparatus.
Retract scalp and drill a burr hole 1 mm anterior and 1.5 mm lateral to bregma.
Inject 50,000 NPA or NPD cells suspended in 1 μL DMEM F-12 without FBS into a pocket spanning 3 mm–3.5 mm deep in the striatum.
Seal the skull with bone wax and scalp with sutures.
Reverse anesthesia using atipamezole at 1 mg/kg via intraperitoneal injection, followed by additional analgesia from buprenorphine at 0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously.
Observe mice until they are bright, alert, and responsive before returning them to normal housing.
Before animal tumor burden reaches the humane endpoint, euthanize the animal and remove its brain.
Assess tumor burden with behavioral monitoring (hunched posture, scruffy fur, lack of ambulation, periocular porphyrin staining).
For time-lapse imaging, mice should nearly reach the moribund stage.
Consistently perform weekly imaging using IVIS.
Pipette 100 μl of Matrigel solution onto cell culture inserts and incubate for 1 h before sample acquisition.
Add 1 ml of secondary mouse culture medium to avoid desiccation of the Matrigel.
Pipette 1,000 μL of the laminin coating solution onto cell culture inserts in a six well plate.
Incubate for 1 hour.
Melt 4% (m/v) agarose in the microwave until it begins to boil and becomes transparent.
Place melted agarose in a 40°C water bath to prevent solidification.
Pipette 50 mL of human culture medium into a 50 mL conical tube.
Warm the medium to 37°C.
In the laminar flow hood, place the container of sectioning medium in an ice bucket.
Oxygenate the medium with 95% O2 and 5% CO2 gas using plastic tubing and a sterile 10 mL pipette for at least 20 minutes.
Prepare 30 mL of cold, oxygenated human culture medium into a 50 mL conical tube.
Place the prepared medium in an ice bucket until collection.
Put the mouse under anesthesia via inhalation using Fluriso™.
Place the mouse in the gas anesthesia system anesthesia chamber.
Turn the 100% oxygen tank on to between 345 and 448 kPa.
Adjust the airflow to the anesthesia chamber to 1.5 L per minute.
Set the anesthesia vaporizer to 0.25%.
Wait 1–2 min for the mouse to lose consciousness.
Turn off the oxygen, airflow, and vaporizer before removing the mouse.
Place the mouse on a sterile surface in the biological safety cabinet.
Spray the head and neck of the mouse with 70% ethanol to wet the fur.
Euthanize the mouse via decapitation with the large surgical scissors.
Place the head in a 10 cm Petri dish, covered.
Transport the head on ice to the laminar flow hood.
Open the scalp rostral to caudal using the large surgical scissors.
Dissect the brain using rongeurs.
Squeeze until separation of the frontal bones is observed upon breaking the interfrontal suture.
Remove any muscle and cervical vertebrae from the caudal side of the head with the rongeurs.
Begin removing the bones of the skull from rostral to caudal.
Once the dorsal surface of the brain is fully exposed, remove it from the skull.
Cut the cranial nerves on the ventral side with the small surgical scissors.
Gently dislodge the olfactory bulbs with forceps.
Acquire human high grade glioma samples immediately after surgery from the operating room.
Avoid necrotic regions when acquiring samples.
Place acquired samples in cold, oxygenated culture medium on ice for transportation.
Embed tumor specimens in 4% agarose to generate semi-rigid blocks for sectioning.
Ensure agarose is less than or equal to 37°C before embedding to prevent tissue damage.
Pipette approximately 10 ml of 4% (m/v) agarose into an embedding mold, avoiding bubbles and ensuring enough room for sample submersion.
Submerge the sample in the agarose using forceps.
Hold the sample in place with a 10 μL pipet tip until the agarose has cooled and become viscous enough to hold the tissue but not yet solidified.
Cut the corners of the truncated 12 × 12 mm embedding mold with a single-sided razorblade.
Remove the agarose block from the mold.
Glue the agarose block to the specimen disc with cyanoacrylate adhesive.
Allow the glue to set for 5-8 minutes on ice.
Trim the bottom of the agarose block at an angle with a single-sided razor blade if tissue orientation is misaligned.
Trim the agarose block so the blade fixture on the vibratome can advance, depending on the amount of agarose used.
Place a 10 cm Petri dish on ice in the laminar flow hood and fill it with cold, oxygenated sectioning medium.
Clean the double-sided razorblade first with acetone and then with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Carefully break the razorblade in half.
Clamp half of the blade to the knife holder.
Fasten the buffer tray to the vibratome.
Fill the cooling bath outside of the buffer tray with ice.
Change the razorblade between samples when sectioning multiple samples.
Fill the buffer tray with cold, oxygenated sectioning medium to submerge the agarose block.
Run surgical tubing into the laminar flow hood from the tank of 95% O2 and 5% CO2 gas.
Oxygenate the cold sectioning medium in the buffer tray using a pipet tip on the end of the surgical tubing.
Fasten the specimen disc with the attached agarose block to the buffer tray.
Set the section thickness to 250–300 μm on the vibratome.
Adjust the start and stop points of blade advancement according to the position of the agarose block.
Set the knife feed speed and knife sectioning frequency.
Utilize continuous, automatic blade advancement.
Begin sectioning, transferring tissue sections to a Petri dish on ice containing the sectioning medium using a mini perforated spoon.
Separate the agarose from the tissue with forceps.
Remove the six well plate containing the cell culture inserts and the 50 mL conical tube containing the primary mouse culture medium from the incubator.
Place them in the laminar flow hood.
Pipette off the laminin solution from the cell culture inserts.
Wash the laminin-coated cell culture inserts once with DPBS supplemented with magnesium and calcium.
Wash the laminin-coated cell culture inserts twice with warmed primary mouse culture medium.
Transfer the explants to the laminin-coated cell culture inserts.
Pipette enough primary mouse culture medium into the insert to barely cover the explants.
Pipette 2 mL of medium into the bottom of the well outside of the cell culture insert.
Place the six well plate containing the vibrosections plated on the laminin-coated cell culture inserts back in the incubator at 37°C.
After 6-18 hours, transfer the cell culture insert to be imaged to a glass bottom dish using sterile forceps in a laminar flow hood.
Change the media to secondary mouse culture medium.
Add 2 mL of medium per dish and keep it in the incubator for 20 minutes.
Transfer the cell culture inserts to the confocal microscope for time-lapse imaging.
Stain patient-derived brain tumor samples with Hoechst 33342 and Calcein AM.
Incubate the explants for 1.5 hours in a solution containing Hoechst (1:4000) and 2 μM Calcein.
Wash the explants three times with warm human culture medium.
Wash Matrigel®-coated cell culture inserts three times with warm human culture medium.
Transfer the explants to the Matrigel®-coated cell culture inserts in a laminar flow hood.
Pipette enough secondary mouse culture medium to barely cover the explants.
Add 2 mL of medium into the bottom of the well outside of the cell culture insert.
Incubate explants slices in a humidified, temperature and CO2 controlled incubation chamber included as part of a laser scanning confocal microscope for time-lapse imaging.
Start the microscope and set the temperature of the humidified incubation chamber to 37°C.
Turn on the CO2 and set it to 5%.
Place an extra container with sterile water into the incubator chamber.
Transfer the glass bottom dish containing tissue sections into the microscope incubator chamber.
Allow the media in the dish to equilibrate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 15 minutes.
Secure the glass bottom plate to prevent movement of the explant section during imaging.
Select the objective to use for confocal imaging.
Turn on the Argon 488 nm and the DPSS 561 nm excitation lasers.
Set the laser power equally for all positions.
Set laser power to the minimum level possible.
Simultaneously excite GFP+ tumors and Tdtomato+ parenchyma at 488 nm and 561 nm using scan mode: frame; frame size 1024 × 1024 or higher.
Use averaging mode: line for imaging.
Select a position (x,y,z) of interest using ocular observation and the locate function.
Save each selected position.
Set Z stack positions to address 3D analysis of the explant.
Select the first (bottom) and last (top) positions on focus for the explant.
For 2D image scanning, select an intermediate position between the extreme positions of the explants.
Use the Time Series function to set time intervals: usually >300 cycles at an interval of 10 minutes.
Set number of tile scan per location using a 10× objective without tile scan and use 2 × 2 tile scan for a 20× objective.
Select Focus strategy to Autofocus Mode “Fluorescence” for every time and position.
Use AutoSave imaging or Streaming function during the process.
Start running the time lapse scanning imaging.
Perform imaging between 24 and 72 hours.
Place explant on top of inserts in different wells as required.
Apply media with the corresponding treatment into each well.
Remove media after treatment.
Fix tissue in 4% paraformaldehyde for 24–48 hours.
Cryopreserve or paraffin embed fixed tissue for further analysis.
Perform histopathological analysis using H&E staining.
Conduct immunohistochemistry on samples.
Execute immunofluorescence on samples.
Carry out spatial transcriptomic analysis (RNA-Scope) on tissues.
Remove sample dish from the microscope platform after image acquisition.
Remove the secondary mouse culture medium from the cell culture inserts and dish.
Fill the cell culture inserts and dish with 4% PFA.
Secure the lid of the 10 cm Petri dish with parafilm.
Leave the tissue at 4°C for 24–48 h.
Use a pipette to remove as much of the 4% PFA as possible from the Petri dish, discarding it properly.
Wash the tissue sections with DPBS without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ two times.
Transfer tissue to 30% sucrose solution overnight at 4°C.
Prepare a plastic container filled with cold isopentane/2-methylbutane and place into a metal container filled with liquid nitrogen.
Spread a thin layer of OCT media in the bottom of a disposable plastic base mold.
Using a flat micro-spatula, remove the brain from the 30% sucrose solution and transfer an explant from the culture insert onto the OCT coating.
Fill the plastic mold with OCT to assure that the tissue slices are submerged.
Quickly place the cryomold with OCT and the explants into the isopentane/2-methylbutane upon solidification of the OCT, remove the cryomold with the explants in dry ice.
Store it at −80°C.
Melt the 2% (m/v) agarose by swirling and heating until light boiling is observed and the solution becomes transparent.
Place the agarose in a 40°C water bath to maintain its liquid state.
With a micropipette, spread 500 μL of 2% agarose into a thin, even coat in the bottom of a disposable plastic base mold.
Transfer an explant from a cell culture insert onto the agarose bed with a flat micro-spatula.
Fill the plastic mold to fully submerge the tissue slices.
Allow the agarose to solidify at 20°C–25°C.
Carefully remove the agarose block with a microspatula.
Place the agarose block in a labeled tissue MACROSETTE™, sandwiched between two rectangular foam biopsy pads.
Mix MACROSETTES™ with 70% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 30 seconds.
Mix MACROSETTES™ with 80% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 1 minute.
Mix MACROSETTES™ with 95% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 1 minute.
Repeat the previous step of mixing MACROSETTES™ with 95% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 1 minute.
Mix MACROSETTES™ with 100% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 1 minute.
Repeat the previous step of mixing MACROSETTES™ with 100% ethanol under vacuum at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Let MACROSETTES™ drain for 1 minute.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in 100% ethanol at 20°C–22°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 2 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in xylene at 20°C–22°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 1 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in xylene at 20°C–22°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 1 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in xylene at 20°C–22°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 2 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in paraffin at 58°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 2 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in paraffin at 58°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 2 min.
Immerse MACROSETTES™ in paraffin at 58°C under a vacuum for 1 h.
Let drain for 2 min.
Place the MACROSETTES™ in the paraffin bath, tapping them with forceps to allow all bubbles to escape.
Ensure the cold plate is turned on.
Wait 10–15 min or until the agarose blocks within the MACROSETTES™ have become fully transparent.
Remove the agarose block from the MACROSETTE™.
Trim excess agarose away using a single-sided razor blade slowly.
Place the trimmed agarose block in a heated metal mold and transfer to the cold plate.
Press down on the agarose block to adhere it to the metal mold, removing any air bubbles.
Fill the metal mold with liquid paraffin.
Place the corresponding microcassette on top of the mold.
Add enough additional liquid paraffin to fill the microcassette.
Gently transfer the metal mold and microcassette to the cold plate.
Allow the paraffin to solidify.
Once the paraffin is cool to the touch, carefully remove the paraffin block and microcassette.
Section the explants on a microtome at 5 μm.
Mount the sections on slides.
Stain the sections as needed for further experiments including H&E, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and multiplex assays such as RNAScope.
Use Fiji software with the TrackMate plugin for cell tracking.
Launch the start panel in TrackMate and click “Next.”
Select cell size of 20 μm, threshold of 1, and DoG method (Difference of Gaussian detectors) for blob detection.
Click “Next” once progress bar reaches end to proceed to tracking panel.
Use the “Simple LAP” tracker and click “Next.”
Open track filter panel and remove tracks with fewer than 10 spots.
Click the “Analysis” tab and three windows pop up with “Spots”, “Tracks Statistics” and “Link in Track Statistics.”
Use the two CSV files named ”Spots” and “Tracks Statistics” for further analysis.
Filter trajectories using a Gaussian kernel as a filter (with standard deviation σ = 2 and a stencil of 9 points).
Run the script step2_filter_data.jl located in the src folder on GitHub.
Filter individual cell trajectories from time-lapse datasets using the script.
Estimate positions Xi(t) and velocities Vi(t) of cells i.
Deduce velocity direction θi(t) from velocity Vi(t).
Apply filtering to obtain a smooth path for estimating cell velocity at each time step.
Save all filtered trajectories in jld2 files located in the data_tracking folder on GitHub, named as step2_data_filtered.
Investigate cell behavior by applying statistics on velocity angle θ, speed c, and velocity vector v.
Use Fiji to determine the coordinates of specific zones in glioma explants.
Save the x and y coordinates in a JSON file format called “coordinates.json”.
Run the script “step3_zone_create_df.jl” available on GitHub to assign different zones based on the coordinates.
Run the Julia script provided at GitHub to generate data frames for each zone analysis.
Repeat the run twice to execute velocity or correlation analysis.
Change line 13 of the script to "velocity_or_correlation = “velocity”" for velocity analysis.
Change line 13 of the script to "velocity_or_correlation = “correlation”" for correlation analysis.
Generate final graphs using Julia scripts provided at GitHub: use "step3_zone_velocity_plot.jl" for velocity and "step3_zone_correlation_plot.jl" for correlation analysis.
Access angle velocity, speed distribution, and velocity heatmap results in the df velocity folder as pdfs.
Access correlation, nematic correlation, and relative position results in the df correlation folder.
Utilize the collection of angles θi inside a specific zone.
Assess three distributions: (wrapped) Gaussian for a flock, symmetric Gaussian for a stream, and the constant function for a swarm.
Run the R script provided on GitHub to perform likelihood analysis.
Generate the zone distribution graph in R Studio.
Analyze Akaike weight results to determine the highest likelihood.
